title: Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index (January 2027), 10:00 a.m. ET — the last consumer datapoint before the Jan 26-27 FOMC, printed on day one of that meeting
source: EST: the publisher's stated rule, now VERIFIED against five sourced January editions rather than applied blind. conference-board.org/topics/consumer-confidence (fetched direct 2026-09-06, HTTP 200, 332,031 bytes) states "The Conference Board publishes the Consumer Confidence Index (R) at 10 a.m. ET on the last Tuesday of every month" and names its next release as "Tuesday, September 29th at 10 AM ET". Unlike December — where a sibling lane found the rule refuted five-for-five — the January rule holds on every edition this session could source: 2022-01-25 (prnewswire.com/news-releases/consumer-confidence-fell-in-january-301467668.html, HTTP 200, dateline "Jan. 25, 2022 ... 10:00 ET"), 2023-01-31 (named verbatim by the publisher's own CCI-Dec-2022 page, HTTP 200, "The next release is Wednesday, January 31 at 10 AM ET" — the weekday word is the publisher's own error; Jan 31 2023 was a Tuesday), 2024-01-30 (CCI-Dec-2023, HTTP 200, "The next release is Tuesday, January 30th at 10 AM ET"), 2025-01-28 (CCI-Dec-2024, HTTP 200, "Tuesday, January 28th"; corroborated by prnewswire.com/news-releases/us-consumer-confidence-retreated-in-january-302362076.html dateline "Jan. 28, 2025 ... 10:00 ET") and 2026-01-27 (prnewswire.com/news-releases/us-consumer-confidence-fell-sharply-in-january-302671278.html, HTTP 200, dateline "Jan. 27, 2026 ... 10:00 ET"). All five are the last Tuesday of their January. 2027-01-26 is the last Tuesday of January 2027. Kept estimate because no January-2027 announcement exists yet — the Board names each date roughly a month ahead, so late December 2026 settles it — and per this lane's no-self-confirm limit on an event discovered in-sweep. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: Canonical entry written by this id's own never-assessed research (2026-09-06) after reading the single prior proposal (proposals/consumer-confidence-2027-01-26.from-fhfa-hpi-2027-01-26.json, filed by the FHFA lane the same day), which is now inert. THE FINDING THAT CHANGES THIS ENTRY: the proposal named the FHFA HPI print (9:00 ET, same day) as the confound. It is the smaller one. federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm (fetched direct 2026-09-06, HTTP 200) shows the FOMC's January meeting landing on the LAST TUESDAY of January in every year 2021-2027 — 2021-01-26, 2022-01-25, 2023-01-31, 2024-01-30, 2025-01-28, 2026-01-27 and 2027-01-26 — which is the same slot the Conference Board keys to. So every January CB print since 2021 has also been FOMC DAY ONE, and 2027-01-26 will be too (the Fed labels 2027 dates tentative). That gives the date two independent calendar rules pointing at the same day, one of them primary-sourced, which is why this estimate is materially stronger than the December sibling's. It also makes the release day triply confounded (FHFA 9:00 ET, CB 10:00 ET, FOMC convening) and it is the reason no attribution is possible from daily bars. Measured this session on 2021-01-01 -> 2026-09-05 daily bars: FOMC day one is statistically ORDINARY (0 of 9 instruments differ from baseline at p<0.05; nearest XLY p=0.0509), while the very next session — decision day, here 2027-01-27 — is the most extraordinary day on this calendar (8 of 9 at p<0.05; SPY median session range 1.354% vs 0.964%, p=0.0001). The tradable statement therefore belongs to fomc-2027-01-27, not here. Full record, sources, the eight legs and three forward tests: docs/research/events/consumer-confidence-2027-01-26.md. Not a trade: symbols is empty and a re-grep of trade-playbooks.md and multi-symbol-sweep.md for any macro- or sentiment-keyed playbook returns 0 hits (the single 'sentiment' string in trade-playbooks.md is a portfolio-weighting input, not a macro-print playbook). CORRECTION BANKED FOR A SIBLING LANE, not applied by this one (#1449 — a lane never edits another event's file): consumer-confidence-2026-12-22 leg 3 states the December field cut-off is a fixed December 16 on the grounds that only three editions state one. Two more do. The publisher's own CCI-Dec-2022 page (HTTP 200, self-identified 'Source: December 2022 Consumer Confidence Survey') states December 15, and CCI-Dec-2023 (HTTP 200, 'Source: December 2023 Consumer Confidence Survey') states December 14. Five of five state a cut-off and they are Dec 14/15/16, a 6-7 day lag rather than a fixed date. That ledger's dependent claims survive unharmed — a Dec 14 cut-off still closes after the 12-09 FOMC, the 12-10 CPI and the 12-11 CR expiry — but its FT-consumer-confidence-2026-12-22-style 'fixed date' wording is wrong and its own kill switch on a non-12-16 cut-off has effectively already fired.
